# lnurlcash-go

LNURLcash (LUD-25) bearer note client for Go. MIT.

go get github.com/lnurlcash/lnurlcash-go

## CRITICAL: HTTP retries

Every LNURLcash mutation (rotate/split/merge/melt) is an HTTP GET, but is NOT
idempotent - the first attempt burns the input note. net/http retries an
idempotent request sent on a REUSED connection, and a client with no Transport
uses the process-wide http.DefaultTransport pool.

LUD-25 closed this at the service end: a service MUST answer a byte-identical
retried rotate/split/merge with the success it already returned, sig and sig2
included where it gave any.
So Client re-sends a mutation whose answer was lost, on purpose and bounded
(Client.MutationRetries; 0 means the default of one extra attempt, negative
turns it off), and a dropped connection usually resolves into a completed
mutation. NEVER a melt: it carries pr, is paid asynchronously and has no replay
guarantee. Never a definitive refusal. The SAME Request goes out each time -
the replay is matched on the notes the k1s open, p1, p2 and amount, so a fresh
secret would make it a different mutation and a second real burn.

NewClient() still sets DisableKeepAlives: a deliberate retry this package
counts is not the same as an invisible one it does not, and a service that has
not caught up still answers the second attempt as already spent. A
caller-supplied *http.Client SHOULD do the same.

## CRITICAL: every note is a taproot output key Q

LUD-25 (luds 6e865b1): a note is a BIP-341 output key Q, named cp1<Q>, filed
by the mint under hex(Q). A k1 is a SPEND of it:
  64 hex    a bearer note's preimage: short form of the cw1 for the leaf
            OP_SHA256 <h> OP_EQUAL under the BIP-341 NUMS key. Signs nothing,
            so it spends at ANY mint holding the note
  ck1       Q || BIP-340 sig over the key-path sighash of a fixed transaction
            whose prevout is tagged_hash("LNURLcash/mint", domain). Spends at
            THAT mint only. Signing and verifying need the mint's domain
  cw1       leaf, control block, witness; Q recomputed from the control block
An output (p1/p2, a lookup's p, a mint comment) is a cp1 or a bearer note's
hex h = sha256(preimage), the short form of its cp1. NoteIDOf(k1) is hex(Q),
NOT sha256(k1). Domains: any URL or bare host, reduced to the lowercase
hostname (no scheme, no port) by SpendDomainOf.

## CRITICAL: certificates

A mint SHOULD certify every note with a cs1 over hex(Q) and the value, a
bearer note included; a mint with no signer omits it. The tolerant default
accepts an uncertified output named by a bearer h; a received certificate is
passed through.

An output named by a cp1 (p1, or p2 for a split's change) is owed its cs1 in
sig (sig2 for the change) ALWAYS, whatever the Policy - this package's rule,
stricter than LUD-25's SHOULD. Without it ParseMutation returns
*UnverifiableError. That error means the mutation LANDED, so the note is REAL
- persist NewSecrets(err) before anything else (empty from the *WithHash
calls, where the caller named the output). ParseNoteInfo still refuses a
withdrawRequest with no valid mintPubkey.

The zero Policy is the default. Policy{RequireSignatures: true} demands a
certificate for an output named by a bearer h too. Policy{AllowMissingMintPubkey:
true} admits a mint with no mintPubkey. Nothing waives a cp1's cs1.

## API

client := lnurlcash.NewClient()   // fields: HTTP, Timeout, Offline, Secrets

client.FetchNoteInfo(ctx, url) (WithdrawInfo, error)   // MaxWithdrawableMsat is authoritative
client.RotateNote(ctx, callback, k1) (RotatedNote, error)
client.SplitNote(ctx, callback, k1s, amountMsat) (SplitNotes, error)
client.MergeNotes(ctx, callback, k1s) (RotatedNote, error)
client.MeltNote(ctx, callback, k1, pr) (Mutation, error)
client.SettleNote(ctx, baseURL, k1, expectedMsat, sig) (SettledNote, error)
client.ProbeBurnedNote(ctx, url) NoteFate    // NoteLive | NoteGone | NoteFateUnknown
client.FetchPayRequest / RequestInvoice / FetchInvoiceStatus / FetchMintAddress
client.RotateNoteWithHash / SplitNoteWithHash / MergeNotesWithHash (Mutation)
  / RequestMintInvoiceWithHash / FetchNoteInfoByHash
  the caller names each output (a bearer h, or a cp1) - no NewSecrets on
  errors, so persist what the outputs belong to BEFORE calling

DeriveCashRoot(seed) -> CashNode              LUD-25's scheme, BIP-32 m/139'
DeriveCashDomainNode(root, host) -> CashNode  m/139'/d1/d2/d3/d4, d1..d4 =
  HMAC-SHA256(privkey at m/139'/0, host)[0..16] as 4 RAW big-endian uint32.
  RAW: BIP-32 reads >= 2^31 as hardened, so ~half the levels are, decided by
  the host name. NEVER mask the top bit, NEVER harden all four - either
  derives a different tree and restores nothing, silently.
  The domain node IS the key-path notes' address branch. Bearer preimages are
  plain randomness (GenerateNoteSecret), never seed-derived.
CashNodeToHex / CashNodeFromHex   privateKey || chainCode, 64 bytes
DeriveCashChild(node, rawUint32)  BIP-32 CKDpriv, for checking this package
  against BIP-32's own vectors
DeriveNoteRoot / DeriveNoteSecret  LEGACY pre-spec HMAC scheme. Do not mint
  under it; still scanned so old notes stay findable.
BuildNoteInfoURLByHash(withdrawLink, h) + ParseNoteInfoByHash(body, policy)
  the ?p= informational GET (h a cp1 or a bearer h), so a restore walk keeps
  spends off the wire. Unknown and BURNED are one answer.
DeriveCashMaster(seed) -> CashNode  BIP-32 m, for paths this package does not name

Spends (spend.go):
VerifySpend(k1, domain) -> VerifiedSpend{OutputKey, Legacy, Unevaluated}
  opens which Q at this mint, as a mint would, time claims aside. Legacy: an
  old ck1 (fixed message, or 65-byte ECDSA) - rotate it. Unevaluated: a cw1
  whose leaf is not a bearer hashlock - structure, Q and leaf rules only
DecodeSpend(k1) -> Spend{Kind, OutputKey, Signature, ScriptPath}  no checking
NoteIDOf(k1) -> hex(Q)   compare notes by this, NEVER by k1. Names, does not verify
NoteLookupOf(k1) -> a bearer preimage's h, else cp1<Q>; for FetchNoteInfoByHash
SpendDomainOf(url or host) -> lowercase hostname
SpendPrevout(domain), SpendSigMsg(Q, domain, locktime, sequence, leaf or nil),
  KeyPathSighash(Q, domain), ScriptPathSighash(Q, domain, leaf, lt, seq)
  SIGHASH_DEFAULT, input 0, hand-rolled; spec vector 3 pins every field
TapLeafHash(script, version), TaprootTweak(P, merkleRoot) -> (Q, oddY),
  OutputKeyOf(script, controlBlock) -> Q (merkle fold, tweak, parity CHECKED),
  IsXOnlyPoint(x), NumsKey, TapleafVersion (0xc0)
BearerLeaf(h), BearerNoteOf(h) -> {OutputKey, ControlBlock, Leaf},
  BearerNoteID(hex h) -> hex(Q), BearerCw1(preimage) -> the full cw1
Cw1{Locktime, Sequence, Script, ControlBlock, Witness}; EncodeCw1 / DecodeCw1
  (structure only) / IsCw1 / OutputKeyOfCw1. Big-endian u32 u32 (u16 len item)*
CheckLeafPolicy(version, script) - refuses leaf version != 0xc0 and any
  OP_SUCCESSx outside pushed data
CheckTimeClaim(locktime, sequence, now, lockedAt) - the mint's clock rules
  (Unix-time locktime only, BIP-68 time-type relative locks only); custodial
No script interpreter.

Key-path notes (recoverable.go):
DeriveCashAddressNode(root, host) -> CashNode  m/139'/d1/d2/d3/d4, hashing key
  m/139'/0: the spec's literal path, the same node DeriveCashDomainNode returns
CashNodeToCx1(node) -> Cx1{PubkeyXOnly, ChainCode}  watch-only; links the branch
DeriveNotePubkey(branchX, chainCode, i) -> [32]byte  Q, used as is (no BIP-86
  tweak); watch-only; i any uint32
DeriveNoteSecretKey(branchKey, chainCode, i) -> [32]byte  negates an odd branch
  key first. t = tagged_hash("LNURLcash/derive", P || cc || ser32_be(i));
  t is reduced mod n; a key at zero is an ERROR (use the next index)
SignNoteOwnership(sk, domain) -> [96]byte  Q || BIP-340 sig over
  KeyPathSighash(Q, domain), zero aux_rand: one deterministic ck1 per mint
RecoverNoteOwnershipPubkey(payload, domain) -> NoteOwnership{PubkeyXOnly,
  Legacy}  verifies before returning: the domain's sighash, else the old
  fixed messages (Legacy); a 65-byte ECDSA payload is recovered (Legacy)
EncodeCp1 / DecodeCp1 (32 bytes, MUST be a curve point), EncodeCk1 (96),
  Cx1 (64), IsCp1/IsCk1/IsCx1
DecodeCk1 -> DecodedCk1{Current [96]byte, Legacy [65]byte, IsLegacy}; .Bytes()
  bech32m, NO 90-char limit, all-uppercase ok; mixed case, a bech32 checksum,
  a wrong hrp or length, or non-zero padding are refused. Never panic
EncodeCs1WithAmount / DecodeCs1WithAmount / IsCs1WithAmount
  current certificate: Cs1{AmountMsat, Signature}; HRP is "cs" plus the
  BOLT11 amount suffix. EncodeCs1 / DecodeCs1 / IsCs1 are LEGACY fixed-HRP.
  DecodeAnyCs1 / IsAnyCs1 accept either during migration.
Wire: a spend goes wherever a k1 does. An output (cp1 or bearer h) goes as
  p1/p2 on rotate/split/merge, p on a lookup, the comment on a mint invoice
  (a bearer h also as h). An off-curve cp1 is refused before sending.
Certificates (signature.go), cs1 over "LNURLcash:<amount_msat>:<hex(Q)>":
  VerifyNoteSignature(k1, domain, amountMsat, sig, mintPubkey) -> Certification
    checks k1 opens Q at domain first; a bearer note falls back to its h
  VerifyNoteSignatureHash(h, ...)       a bearer note by its h: Q, then h
  VerifyNoteSignatureForKey(hexQ, ...)  a watcher with no spend
  VerifyNoteURL(noteURL, mintPubkey) -> (amountMsat, Certification)
  Certification: CertifiedOverQ | CertifiedOverHash (pre-taproot mint) |
    NotCertified; .Verified()
  NoteSignatureMessage(k1, amt), NoteSignatureMessageForHash(hexID, amt),
    and the Digest pair: the message over a note's hex id
DeriveNostrCashSeed(sk) / DeriveNostrAddressNode(sk, host)  EXTENSION, not
  LUD-25: seed = HMAC-SHA256(sk, "LNURLcash/nostr-seed"), then the path above
AddressProofMessage(action, domain, username) / AddressProofDigest(...)
  / SignAddressProof(indexZeroSK, action, domain, username) -> [64]byte
  raw BIP-340 over sha256("LNURLcash:<register|unregister>:<domain>:<username>")

Pure functions: VerifyNoteSignature, VerifySpend, GenerateNoteSecret, HashK1, IsPreimage,
ResolveNoteInput, ResolveMintInput, ResolveLnurlInput, IsAllowedServiceURL,
BuildNoteURL, WithNewK1, WithoutK1, NoteK1, NoteDeclaredAmountMsat,
NoteSignature, ParseMintFee, ApplyMintFee, GrossUpForMintFee, DescribeMintFee,
DecodeBolt11AmountMsat, IsBolt11Invoice, SameInvoice.

No-I/O protocol layer: RotateRequest / SplitRequest / MergeRequest /
MeltRequest / NoteInfoRequest / InvoiceRequest / VerifyRequest return
Request{URL, NewSecrets}; ParseNoteInfo(body, queriedURL, Policy) /
ParseMutation(body, request, MutationKind, Policy) / ParseInvoice /
ParseVerify / ParsePayRequest / ParseMintAddress read the body.
ParseMutation takes the Request back and reads which outputs were cp1 off its
URL (p1/p2), so a Request{URL, NewSecrets} rebuilt from persisted fields keeps
the rule.
MutationKind is MutationMelt / MutationRotate / MutationSplit / MutationMerge
and says what the response owes - a melt mints nothing and owes no signature.

Amounts are int64 milli-satoshis everywhere.

## Errors

errors.Is(err, ErrRequestRefused)  nothing sent, note untouched
errors.Is(err, ErrNotePending)     a melt is in flight - retry, NOT spent
IsSpent(err)                       authoritative: already burned
errors.Is(err, ErrOutputInUse)     "already in use": a p1/p2 is taken. Nothing
                                   burned; name a fresh output (next index)
IsUnknownNote(err)                 service does not recognise it
IsAmbiguous(err)                   outcome UNKNOWN - assume nothing
IsUnverifiable(err)                the mutation LANDED, but a cp1 output came
                                   back without its cs1 (or a hash unsigned,
                                   under RequireSignatures). The note is REAL;
                                   only its verifiability is missing
NewSecrets(err)                    the secrets carried by ANY error that could
                                   describe a mutation the service applied:
                                   ambiguous, unverifiable, spent or unknown
*ProtocolError                     a non-mutating response did not match the
                                   spec, incl. a withdrawRequest with no
                                   mintPubkey (unless AllowMissingMintPubkey)

## Rules

1. MaxWithdrawableMsat is the ONLY authoritative value; a note URL's amount is a claim.
2. The wallet generates replacement secrets; never accept a service-supplied k1.
   A ck1 is per mint: sign it for the mint's own domain.
3. On ANY error from a mutation: persist NewSecrets(err) FIRST, then
   ProbeBurnedNote. Not just IsAmbiguous - a spent/unknown refusal and an
   unverifiable one carry them too.
4. A melt's success means IN FLIGHT. ErrNotePending means retry, not spent.
5. Rotate immediately after claiming a minted note.
6. Never log note URLs - the spend is in the query string.

## Conformance

https://github.com/lnurlcash/lnurlcash-conformance
